gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Megrim draws every angular stroke as a thin, measured line, like a futuristic wire bent into letters. Noto Sans Tangsa is the one that does the talking, a sans-serif with wide, inviting round letters and short ascender stems.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-tc: Megrim looks like glowing tubing bent at sharp angles. Noto Sans TC, a sans-serif, handles the heavy lifting with large open counters in a, e and s, while the display face just supplies the futuristic attitude.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Noto Sans Telugu reads crisp and businesslike, with a high midline. Its counters stay connected to the outside, so a long block of text flows along without clogging, while Megrim keeps to a thin outline.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Noto Sans Thaana reads welcoming and open, with wide channels leading into each counter and big lowercase forms. Megrim does angular, rod-like drama best; the sans does easy reading.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-thai: Approachable is the first word for Noto Sans Thai, whose lowercase swells like inflated glass beads and leaves its round letters open, set under Megrim's sharp, uniform-weight lines. The plain sans is the soft, friendly half.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-thai-looped: Megrim looks cut from strips of equal width, all angles and future. Noto Sans Thai Looped, a sans-serif, has tall bodies that look bold and spacious gaps at curve terminals, so paragraphs keep a clean, steady pace.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-tifinagh: Megrim's glyphs look like a ribbon of constant width folded into angular shapes. Noto Sans Tifinagh follows with rounded, open bowls that fill the line like inflated shapes, so long reading feels clean and unhurried.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Noto Sans Tirhuta reads contemporary and clean, with a dominant x-height. Terminals cut back to leave big gaps, so a long passage moves smoothly, while Megrim keeps its own quiet, level beat up top.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Thin as rope and sharply angular, Megrim has no thick or thin parts anywhere. Noto Sans Ugaritic, a sans-serif, sits close between x-height and cap height, with open mouths like a chalk arc left unjoined, so the headline looks wiry above it.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-vai: Megrim brings tubular, wire-like letterforms with an angular, futuristic edge. Noto Sans Vai, a modern sans, lets words read as solid blocks with generous space between curve ends and stems, so a long passage feels approachable.
